summary: I am returning to this project after a few months focusing on other projects in the day job.
text:
I am returning to this project after a few months focusing on other projects in the day job. I have sharpened many AI Engineering skills and could potentially capitalize on my disconnection from the work to provide a fresh perspective where before I may have gotten stuck on unimportant issues. I need you to review recent open claude code sessions looking for workstreams that remain open. I was basically using the workstream skill for those, but cant remember. I lost my vscode claude code tabs with CC sessions that I used to use to bring myself up to speed on open workstreams. Ideally I would just use Jira for that (I believe it was the FD-264 epic?) but I don't remember maintaining it as a strict dashboard-like single source of truth.

I'll tell you my recollection, but then you need to use a simple adversarial review to get objective about it. Use timestamps on worktrees, jsonl transcripts, jira issues, etc, along with jira issue statuses to infer what was last worked on.

Ultimately my goal here is to re-establish project development direction as we enter into the Fall and I resume the app seminar and working group. I have my now somewhat cleaned intuition and motiviation after 2-3 months of break about what to do next, but that has to be balanced with whatever careful detailed work was in flight when I last left it.

My clean intuition and motivation today is that chatting with the personal app works reasonably well and offers insights on the user's personal SARF history just from the chat itself, but that I have only really tested it with a single conversation. We wrote code to handle multi-session extraction, but at the same time I don't remember actually testing returning to a diagram file, starting a new session, and chatting with it and having it add any new data to the diagram, to see if that works but also get a sense of how it *feels* to do that. I think that is an ideal state and achievement, to at least be able to start conversations at will when new thoughts come to mind about my own functioning or important new life events happen, I need to be able to chat about them while they are happening, like after a few days or weeks or even months, to capture data in a long horizon fashion over years of returning and chatting.

Additionally, I do remember that a major hangup to having professional therapist beta testers from the app seminar try the app out was that the family diagram part was not very effective. We were making incremental improvements on that but it was a very difficult problem and its hard to tell when I was stuck in a rabbit hole in each workstream toward improving diagram generation. Maybe diagram generation is one of those features that can just start out terrible but at least the chat is useful in itself and the timeline generation is so novel that people will accept mediocre performance. I don't know...

For timeline extraction/generation, my intuition is that ground truth has been too sparse and synthetic to get past our extraction cieling. Even with the recent F1 improvement from the gemini flash upgrade, those scores are only as good as the ground truth. So over the past few months, I've been sort of reflecting about the possibility of creating a second generation of ground truth around real cases like my own chat cases and then also the chat cases of the Beta testers were the people in the working group. Maybe that can create some sort of a feedback loop betweenthem finally Beta testing the app and chatting with it and then generating more realistic data for us to code and using the IRR study. Of course, the IRR participants using their own content can create all kinds of problems with objectivity, but at the same time that is the tradition in Bowen theory and there is a precedent for it. I don't think thatthat tradition ever produced any valid and reliable data when people were working with their own families but at the same time, they were usually doing self case studies and not a formal IRR review process with a mechanized data extraction system like we're building here. So it's a consideration.

Anyway, that's a lot. The mantra here has always been to keep it very simple but at the same time this project seems like one that's inherently complicated and we actually have to reinvent the wheel, like going from 0 to one for the first time, before I can actually get an MVP into the App Store. I leave that up for debate.I would just really love to be able to pick up the app and free associate when things are going on in my life and also generate data at the same time. And it would be great. I guess if the other Bethe testers were doing that too and then we automatically had a bunch of more realistic data to code. I like that idea. But I don't wanna ignore the detailed work streams that were in flight and I lost all my history. So go back and do an assessment of this project and help me figure outthe direction for the next nine months in this academic year. This is a brainstorming and planning phase and I need you to record it.

I wonder if there is some way to add an agentic loop or chat agent into the personal and pro apps just for beta testing. Like something that guides and/or collects feedback or makes it more fun or feel more productive for the beta testers? I have no idea what thgat could look like. I am just trying to think of ways to offload a lot of the momentum here to AI while keeping human oracle both from me and the beta testers in front and center. And maybe the same thing with the training app when coding cases. At my day job in Micron I built in a MCP build door to my agentic workflows enging that has many primitives to add agents and workflows, edit the python code for tool calls, get runtime logs, everything an engineer user would do to author debug control and monitor agentic workflows, including one tool call that included a massive comprehensive reference manual that make claude code intelligent about the engine and how to build and debug etc. The pattern has worked incredibly well. This made it so users aren't aiming claude code at a source tree for the app/engine and asking it to do its best developing in that framework. Instead they are just describing what they want their workflows to do and claude code is handling the rest. They still have to be technical and we are still ironing out the user experience there to go even further along that frictionless vector, but it's been an awesome innovation. My own beta testers are highly untechnical so can't use claude code or anything. But the point is that their UI became a chat agent which raised the altitude to allow them to think and chat closer to the altitude of their own subject matter expertise instead of twiddling with the technical details of the code and framework. They get to focus on the task at hand. The biggest problem with my user base for Family Diagram has always been that the tools are too technical to use, and the userbase is really not technical.
